name: system.apps.defaults
description: Return the OS-registered default app for URL schemes and file extensions (e.g. which browser opens `https`, which app opens `.pdf`). Omit `keys` for a curated set of common protocols and extensions. Keys with no registered handler are left out. Read-only.

keys.description: Protocols and extensions to resolve. An extension is `.` followed by 1 to 32 characters from A-Z, a-z, 0-9, `_` and `-`, with no further dots. A protocol is a URI scheme (RFC 3986): a letter followed by zero or more letters, digits, `+`, `.` or `-`, with no trailing colon. Any other key returns `invalid_args` (for example `.`, `.tar.gz`, `http:`, `foo/bar`).

key.description: The requested protocol or extension, echoed as given.

name.description: Friendly name of the handler, e.g. `Google Chrome`.

exe.description: Absolute path of the handler executable. Omitted when the handler does not resolve to an executable, which is typical for Store app handlers.

x-implementations.name: assoc_query_string_w
x-implementations.description: `AssocQueryStringW` with `ASSOCSTR_FRIENDLYAPPNAME` and `ASSOCSTR_EXECUTABLE` per key. Protocol keys (no leading dot) pass `ASSOCF_IS_PROTOCOL` so the user's default-app choice is honoured; extension keys pass no flag.

x-implementations.name: assoc_query_string_a
x-implementations.description: `AssocQueryStringA` from shlwapi (Windows 2000, or any system with IE5 installed). ANSI results transcoded to UTF-8 by the agent.

windows-modern.description: AssocQueryStringW. `ASSOCF_IS_PROTOCOL` (Windows 8+) is required for protocol keys: without it `http` resolves through `HKCR\http\shell\open\command` and ignores the user's choice. The agent may also pass `ASSOCF_APP_TO_APP` (Windows 10 1803+) so packaged handlers resolve a friendly name; without it a Store handler may come back with no usable `name` and is then left out.

windows-classic.description: AssocQueryStringA when shlwapi exports it; otherwise the verb is not advertised. There is no `ASSOCF_IS_PROTOCOL` on these systems, so protocol keys resolve from the `HKCR\<scheme>\shell\open\command` registration.
